Judy Hodges from IDC stated that the deal is merely an illustration of the evolving technological trends in the enterprise software sector.
"We're seeing a major shift in the overall industry in the last 18 to 24 months," she said. "A few years ago, most vendors were focused on developing systems around fixed assets, and then manufacturers would integrate [financial, accounting, and manufacturing software] to bring things together...But, now, it's just the opposite" with vendors becoming more horizontal.
David Miller, senior vice president of product management at PeopleSoft, stated that the company aims to offer solutions covering the entire enterprise—all accessible through the Internet, including manufacturing, accounting, customer service, and support.
"Our goals are to be [a solutions provider] across the whole enterprise, as well as three levels down in...manufacturing, to deliver both flexibility and cost-effectiveness," Miller said.
IDC's Hodges noted that customers have increasingly requested this level of business integration from suppliers, with some already adopting open architecture setups offered by firms like IBM, Sun Microsystems, and Microsoft.
"Relieving the pressure to integrate and bringing the business forward is playing a key role in getting the [vertical industries] together as well," Hodges said, referring to vertical industries such as retail, financial services, and shipping. "Traditionally, these [verticals] didn't work together or share information, but now, they've started to join up," she said, emphasizing that horizontal customer relationship management is the new frontier.
Nancy Hughes, vice president of Industry Marketing at SAP Americas, stated that the complexity of integrating various enterprise components over the Internet or extranet has effectively created opportunities for solution providers and developers. She noted that traditional software providers do not possess the necessary resources to develop this type of extensive front office and back office solutions, and they are expecting solution providers to take this role instead.
